newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat, mkt awaits U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat, mkt awaits U.S. data.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed unchanged at 19.25 percent on Monday after what traders said was a quiet session for a market awaiting key U.S. economic data later in the week.
"It was very quiet, but the market felt a little under pressure from Wednesday's central bank cutoff date and U.S. data due this week,' a trader said.
Banks have by Wednesday to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with Banco de Mexico.

Dealers said they would closely observe U.S. economic data for indications of possible overheating and the extent of possible hikes in U.S. interest rates at the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

Traders said overnight Cetes rates had reached as high as 19.50 percent during the session in response to early softness on the peso, but eased off towards the close on buying spurred by a recovery in the peso and stable U.S. long bond yields.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 1.7 centavos firmer at 7.9090/7.9120 per dollar. U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were meanwhile up 2/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
"The (U.S.) long bond held firm, as did the peso, which both helped rein in the increase in overnight rates," another trader said.
Overnight rates on bank paper for their part ended up 10 basis points at 20.60 percent.
On the Chicago mercantile Exchange, June Cetes futures meanwhile closed up seven centavos to 78.27 pesos.
Liquidity of 179 million pesos was programmed to return to the system on Tuesday from prior central bank participation.
